label: Exit strategy
summary: Exit strategy, as Maaike uses it, refers to the deliberate and extended process of stepping back from corporate employment to assess what you actually want from work and life. It is not a sudden decision but a slow, conscious detachment from corporate identity and external expectations. Central to it is building enough financial runway to make the leap feel survivable rather than reckless.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike frames exit strategy as something both psychological and practical. On the psychological side it means dis-attaching from a corporate identity and the self-worth tied to it, and asking honest questions about energy, motivation and what activities feel natural versus forced. On the practical side it means reducing your salary to a minimum, saving the rest, and building what she calls an emergency exit account with a concrete goal: one year of living costs so you can figure out what comes next without panic. The two sides have to happen together; the financial cushion creates the mental space, and the mental work helps you figure out how little you actually need.
open_questions: The passage cuts off mid-sentence, so it is unclear what Maaike concluded about how deliberate versus accidental the process of finding her new direction actually was.
She mentions that building communities helped her reshape her core business, but the exit strategy section does not explain how that connection formed.
